extraction.notes: Read in full. The source is an activity report (the register notes it as weak monitoring evidence), so most claims are the Foundation's statements about its own projects, and few are findings about the state of technology policy in North Macedonia. Left out as outside the theme under the materiality test: disinformation, fact-checking, media financing and journalism training, including the uses of AI in fact-checking and in disinformation (pages 7-18, 30); the Openness Index on institutional transparency, with its scores (pages 19-24), which is not about a digital issue; digital safety and cyber-hygiene training for civil society (pages 28-29); the UN Cybercrime Convention call (page 25), since cybercrime law enforcement is out; the Global Digital Compact inputs (page 30), which are global and name no North Macedonian measure; media appearances and conference listings that make no claim (pages 30-32), including interviews on slow digitalisation and on digitalisation against corruption, whose content is not given; the forum on digitalisation of services as a mechanism against corruption (page 20), whose content is not given. Digital skills are left out unless linked to a recommendation (item -0013 is flagged). No foreign-worker or Chapter 2 material appears in the report. Where the report refers to analyses (e-services, the Digital Services Act, AI), it gives few or no results; the underlying documents are not in the register. Second-pass check done (G3 condition 2).
